transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I keep jumping into big plans and trips without thinking, and it’s starting to cause problems for my family. My wife got so worried after I recently took off on a long drive without telling anyone that she insisted I come in to talk to someone.

Before this recent period, have you ever had a time lasting at least a couple of weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest in almost everything? Or has it mainly been times of unusually high energy and impulsive behavior without any major depressive episodes?

I don't recall ever having a period where I felt deeply depressed or lost interest in things for weeks at a time. This recent phase of high energy, constant planning, and making impulsive decisions is completely new to me, and it's what is causing all the trouble.

Before this recent high-energy period, have you ever had any earlier episodes like this—times when you needed much less sleep, felt unusually confident or irritable, talked more, or acted impulsively for several days or longer? Or is this the first time anything like this has ever happened?

No, this is the very first time I have ever experienced anything like this. I have always been known for my steady, calm presence until this past month when everything suddenly changed. Before this, I never had these kinds of intense bursts of energy or impulsive behaviors.

During this high-energy period, have you had experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or believing you have special powers or an important mission? Have these beliefs felt completely real to you?

No, I haven't heard or seen things that aren't there, and I don't believe I have any special powers. However, I have felt lately like I'm the only one who really knows how to get things done around here, which makes me impatient with others.

During this high-energy period, for about how many days in a row have you had these changes, and have they been present most of the day nearly every day? Have they been severe enough to cause major problems at work or home, or lead to hospitalization?

This has been going on nearly every day for about a month, starting right after my supervisor pushed me to set a firm retirement date. I haven't been hospitalized, but it has caused major problems like missing mentoring commitments, upsetting my church leaders, and scaring my family by disappearing on long drives to the point my wife feels she can't rely on me.

This is most consistent with a manic episode without psychotic symptoms.
